caption:
The fate of the 15th Amendment to the Constitution is about to be decided. The Supreme Court's verdict is set for Thursday.

A four-member Appellate Division bench, led by the Chief Justice, has concluded hearings on the appeal against the High Court's ruling on the 15th Amendment to the Constitution.

The court has scheduled the verdict for Thursday, July 9, after hearing all parties involved in the case.

During the hearings, lawyer Badiul Alam, representing the appellant Sujon Sompadok, 'fraudulent' and argued that the amendment amendment should be completely abolished.

Conversely, the lawyer for Jamaat-e-Islami, Shishir Monir, argued that a total repeal of the amendment would create a crisis, suggesting instead a partial cancellation of certain parts.

The case follows a High Court ruling on December 17, 2024, which declared parts of the 15th Amendment unconstitutional and canceled them.

The High Court's decision had previously opened a path for the return of the caretaker government system, mesma same as some complexities remained, leading to three separate appeals against the ruling.

headline_marked: Rain and waterlogging: [[CU suspends classes and exams]] for today
headline: Rain and waterlogging: CU suspends classes and exams for today
summary: University of Chittagong has halted all academic activities due to severe weather conditions and flooding on campus.
details: The University of Chittagong (CU) has suspended all classes and examinations for today due to bad weather.
Heavy rainfall and subsequent waterlogging across the campus led to the decision to halt academic activities.
The university administration announced the suspension to ensure the safety and convenience of students and staff.
Students had been facing difficulties navigating the campus as several areas became inundated with rainwater.
caption:
Classes and exams halted! 🌧️ University of Chittagong suspends academic activities today due to heavy rain and waterlogging.

The University of Chittagong (CU) has suspended all classes and examinations for today due to bad weather.

Students had been facing difficulties navigating the campus as several areas became inundated with rainwater.
